text: The directional derivative of a differentiable function f in the direction of a unit vector u is:
choices: the cross product of grad f with u
the Hessian of f applied to u
the dot product grad f . u
the magnitude |grad f|, independent of u
explanation: For a differentiable function, D_u f = grad f . u. It is maximized (giving |grad f|) when u aligns with the gradient, but for a general direction it is the projection grad f . u. The cross product and Hessian are the wrong operations.
